The graph $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of three line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $4$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-5,-2],$ the line segment for $x\in (-2,-1],$ the line segment for $x\in (-1,1],$ and the line segment for $x\in (1,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-2].$    The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-2,-1].$   The corresponding region is a triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-1,1].$   The corresponding region is a triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,4].$   The corresponding region is a rectangle below the $x$-axis, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{4}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}-{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =6+\frac{1}{2}-2-3 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
